messages:
Noah: Quick thread 20m about connector token affinity & exchange patterns. We keep seeing connector owners rely on long-lived project-0 keys + proxying which blows up auditability and tenant isolation. Need concrete alternatives.
Asha: Can we require connectors to do token-exchange into per-tenant ephemeral tokens? Pattern: upstream system holds a long-lived connector identity, then calls our token-broker to mint a short-lived tenant-scoped token using `grant_type=connector_delegation`.
Diego: +1. Implementation detail: broker should record `actor_chain` = [connector_id, delegated_actor_id] and return `x-rw-actor-chain` header so downstream services can reconstruct provenance.
Kelsey: What about performance? Token-broker lookups on every request add latency. Suggest: broker issues short-lived JWTs (signed, 60s TTL) with embedded tenant/project and actor_chain to avoid per-request introspect.
Noah: Sounds good. Concern: revocation. If connector is compromised, we need immediate stop. How do we revoke JWTs?
Asha: Option A: keep TTL tiny (30-60s) + publish revocation list that services check every N seconds. Option B: use reference tokens with cache-forwarding: service caches introspection for token until expiry but checks revocation stamps on miss.
Diego: Tradeoffs: reference tokens allow instant revoke but need cache invalidation; self-contained JWTs are cheap but revocation window = TTL. For connectors, prefer 30s JWTs + short-circuit kill switch in broker + push invalidation via a fast pubsub channel for critical revokes.
Kelsey: Also: ensure the JWT includes `scope` claim with per-route permissions (e.g., `routes:[/v1/ingest,/v1/metrics]`) so services can enforce route-level checks without global roles.
Noah: How to migrate existing long-lived project-0 keys? We need a migration playbook.
Asha: Migration plan: 1) inventory keys that impersonate tenants via project-0. 2) For each connector owner, create connector identity + register allowed tenant list. 3) Run a 2-week shadow mode where broker mints ephemeral tokens and services accept both legacy and new tokens (log-only). 4) After 2w, flip enforcement for pilot connectors. 5) Full cutover w/ support opt-in for Dedicated customers.
Diego: Tooling: `rwctl broker introspect --key KEY` to show derived tenants, last-used routes, and a `rwctl broker migrate --connector-id CID --generate-credentials` for ops to generate the connector identity and sample exchange flow.
Kelsey: Auditing: attach `orig_key_id` and `connector_identity` to every access event and store actor_chain as a structured string. For compliance we must keep the resolved-permission snapshot at time of access.
auth-bot: policy check: new broker flow must include `consent` flag for tenant-scoped data access per legal guidance.
Noah: Edge-case: connectors that legitimately need to call multiple tenants in a single request (multi-tenant aggregator). Pattern: broker can issue a multi-tenant token containing an `aud` array and per-tenant subclaims, but require explicit opt-in and stronger review (security + product).
Asha: For aggregator tokens, require `x-rw-audit-proof` signature that includes request digest so downstream can't replay cross-tenant calls. Also limit expiry to 15s.
Diego: We should update SDKs to provide `exchange()` helpers, sample middleware that attaches `x-rw-actor-chain` and handles retry around short TTLs.
Kelsey: Observability: emit `auth.broker.issue` and `auth.broker.revoke` metrics, plus `auth.token.expiry_skips` when services accept expired tokens in shadow mode. Create a dashboard showing token types and revocation latencies.
infra-bot: deploy note 2835012400 canary of broker v2 with JWT short-ttl support started on eng-runtime, 4% hosts.
Noah: OK next actions: Asha to draft RFC with token formats, revocation channels, and migration playbook. Diego to prototype `rwctl` subcommands and sample SDK middleware. Kelsey to list audit storage schema changes. We'll sync in 1w. :white_check_mark:
